question: Can one public procurement record support a defensible like-for-like unit-price comparison, and what exact evidence would distinguish overpricing from defective pricing or fraud?

resource_budget.boundaries: One finite research result; return partial coverage and access failures honestly.

publication_scope: Public methods, neutral public observations and already published case facts. No new named adverse allegations.
independent_reviewer: root coordinator or another separately identified worker; not the author
required_evidence: Exact source URLs, publication/access dates and page/paragraph/API locators
Raw legal names and stable identifiers kept separate from search normalization
Decimal amounts with payer, period, source measure and basis
At least two plausible alternatives or a specific explanation why only one is testable
Bounded DOJ/OIG/GAO/court novelty search and explicit search limits
A next discriminating observation or a defensible closure/null result
prohibited_inferences: A punctuation difference establishes a fictitious company
A contract ceiling or obligation divided by an estimated quantity establishes a transaction unit price
An anomalous price establishes fraud or recoverable loss
An unsuccessful search proves that a lead is undiscovered
A model-generated answer is an independently verified source
stopping_conditions: Stop on access denial; record the boundary without bypassing it.
Stop the finite cohort at the stated budget; no unattended loop or purchase.
Return no finding when identifiers, product comparability or evidence cannot support one.
Keep any unresolved new named suspicion outside this public repository and return an anonymous summary.
bounded_cohort: One simple, non-sensitive consumable/fastener NSN or exact manufacturer part and revision; no cross-item price ranking. Prefer a current official DLA solicitation with its procurement-history table.
work_steps: Find the original official solicitation/award or a verifiable agency catalog; preserve source and access failure.
Extract separately award ceiling, actual line quantity, unit of issue, unit price and procurement-history dates. If absent, stop the price calculation.
Match exact item and revision, package/unit, quantity tier, condition, delivery, warranty, included testing/engineering and period. Record each mismatch.
Compare only supported pairs; preserve nominal and adjusted values separately and state the adjustment source.
Check the acquisition date, agency and contract clauses before invoking certified cost/pricing rules. Distinguish factual cost-data omissions from market price concerns.
Search published enforcement/audit records for the exact identifier and describe novelty only within that search. Return a null result if comparison fails.
acceptance_tests: At least one inspected primary source or a precisely documented access boundary.
No rate derived from an IDIQ ceiling and estimated annual quantity.
Every comparison states the matched and unmatched terms.
No new fraud label or claimed recovered money.
